title: TypeScript SDK: codec-aware framing helpers for AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams interop
creator: Sofia Chen
description: This ticket implements a small, well-tested set of helpers in the TypeScript SDK to safely convert between AsyncIterator-based streams and WHATWG/Web Streams while preserving framing semantics and codec boundaries. Motivation: we currently see subtle corruption and partial-chunk issues when consumers switch between stream models (e.g., network-delivered byte chunks that split UTF-8 graphemes, JSON tokens, or custom delimiter framing). The helpers will also provide cancel-safe behavior and explicit backpressure propagation so consumers can rely on pause/resume semantics across runtime boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Provide two small public helpers: asyncIteratorToWebStream and webStreamToAsyncIterator with clear TypeScript types and docs.
2) Handled codecs: utf8/text, ndjson (newline-delimited JSON), and raw byte framing (Uint8Array) with explicit boundary APIs.

3) Backpressure semantics preserved: writing to WebStream from AsyncIterator should honor controller.desiredSize equivalents; AsyncIterator consumer should see pull/cancel semantics reflected as awaitable signals.
4) Cancellation is loss-minimizing: partial frames buffered are emitted with an error or handled by a pluggable policy (emit-truncated, drop, or error). Default is error with clear diagnostics.

5) Unit and integration tests covering: grapheme-splitting (multibyte UTF-8), NDJSON objects split across chunks, high-concurrency consumers (2x concurrent readers), and graceful cancellation during a large in-flight payload.
6) Example snippets in README and a small sample repo that demonstrates conversion with fetch() Response.body (WebStream) and a for-await loop consumer.
7) PR reviewed by SDK lead + runtime engineer and merged to main; release note entry in console-2025.03 release.
8) Benchmarks showing negligible overhead for common cases (<2% token throughput regression) and an optional high-performance opt-out API for zero-copy passthrough when no framing is needed.
technical_notes:
Implementation plan:
- Implement a small framing layer with a unified "frame buffer" that collects incoming Uint8Array chunks and exposes a typed readFrame() for codecs.
- Provide codec implementations: Utf8Codec (returns strings, handles multibyte boundaries with TextDecoder streaming), NdjsonCodec (returns parsed objects), RawCodec (returns Uint8Array slices).
- asyncIteratorToWebStream: create a ReadableStream that pulls from the iterator; use controller.enqueue when a frame is available and await backpressure by checking controller.desiredSize; propagate iterator return() to controller.close() and iterator.throw() to controller.error().
- webStreamToAsyncIterator: create an async generator that calls reader.read() in a loop, yields frames through codec, and maps reader.cancel() to generator.return().
- Cancellation policy: default is to throw a FramingError when a partial frame is left on cancel; allow config {onPartial: 'error'|'emit'|'drop'}; include human-friendly message with source (iterator|webstream) and last-seen bytes.
- Type API: keep public surface very small, with overloads that accept generic type T for decoded frame.
- Perf: use TextDecoder with {stream: true} to avoid repeated reallocations. For RawCodec, avoid copying when possible using slice views and a small ring buffer for frame boundaries.
- Testing: fuzz tests to simulate arbitrary chunk splits, property tests for correctness, and a stress harness combining setTimeout-based producers with concurrent consumers to validate backpressure.
decisions: Keep helpers opinionated and small; do not add a full codec catalogue in this change—only implement Utf8, Ndjson, and Raw. Future PRs can add more codecs.
Default partial-frame policy = 'error' to avoid silent data corruption; provide opt-in config for lenient behavior.
Expose a low-level opt-out helper asyncIteratorToWebStreamRaw that does zero-copy passthrough for binary streams with no framing needs.
Do not change existing SDK streaming API surface; these are additive helper utilities in @redwood/sdk/streams.
Performance threshold: helper overhead must be <2% compared to naive passthrough for common text workloads.

test_plan:
Unit tests:
- Utf8Codec handles split multibyte sequences (emoji, combining marks) across random chunk sizes.
- NdjsonCodec reconstructs JSON objects split across boundaries and errors on malformed JSON.
- RawCodec preserves byte identity across conversions.
Integration tests:
- webStreamToAsyncIterator used with fetch() Response.body from a local test server that emits split chunks; consumer is a for-await-of loop parsing NDJSON.
- End-to-end cancel test where consumer cancels mid-frame and assert FramingError is thrown.
- Backpressure test: producer pushes faster than consumer; measure controller.desiredSize behavior and assert that the iterator awaits appropriately.
Performance tests:
- Microbench vs naive passthrough for 1MB text payloads with different chunk sizes.
- Record allocations and wall-time, assert <2% overhead for text workloads.
rollout_plan:
- Merge PR behind feature flag: TF_STREAM_CODEC_ENABLED (default true for SDK releases).
- Publish canary build and run demo app via internal preview; gather perf numbers and smoke tests.
- Once green, cut release for v0.18.0 with release note describing helpers and example usage.
- Follow-up: add a note in SDK migration guide and record a short developer demo video for GitHub examples.
